metadata.question: Was snow present near the Mississippi River Delta Basin (Plaquemines-Balize Delta) during the interval of January 21-24, 2025?

data.raw_code: The question is: "Was snow present near the Mississippi River Delta Basin (Plaquemines-Balize Delta) during the interval of January 21-24, 2025?" This requires detecting snow presence using satellite imagery. I need to: 1. Search strategy: - Location: Mississippi River Delta (Plaquemines-Balize Delta). I'll create a polygon around this area. - Date: January 21-24, 2025 (short 4-day window). - Collection: MODIS snow cover product (MOD10A1) would be ideal for snow detection at daily resolution. Alternatively, Sentinel-2 with NDSI calculation could work but might have cloud issues. 2. Masking strategy: - For MODIS snow cover, we'll use the 'NDSI_Snow_Cover' band which already has quality flags. - Need to handle clouds: MODIS has quality assessment bands. 3. Logic for validation: - Check if collection has images. - Check if any valid pixels after cloud masking. - Determine if snow is present (threshold > 0% snow cover). Let me outline the approach: 1. Define geometry for Mississippi River Delta region. 2. Use MODIS/006/MOD10A1 (Terra Daily Snow Cover) for the date range. 3. Filter by bounds and date. 4. Check collection size. 5. For each image, extract 'NDSI_Snow_Cover' band. 6. Mask out poor quality pixels (values 101-255 represent clouds/no data/water). 7. Calculate mean snow cover percentage over the region. 8. If mean > 0, then snow present. 9. Handle edge cases (no images, no valid pixels, etc.) Alternative: If MODIS has no data, could use Landsat with NDSI calculation, but MODIS is better for daily snow cover. Let me write the code accordingly. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const deltaGeometry = ee.Geometry.Polygon([ [-89.5, 29.0], [-89.0, 29.0], [-89.0, 29.5], [-89.5, 29.5], [-89.5, 29.0] ]); const startDate = '2025-01-21'; const endDate = '2025-01-25'; // exclusive // 2. Data Acquisition - MODIS Snow Cover const modisCol = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/006/MOD10A1') .filterBounds(deltaGeometry) .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .select('NDSI_Snow_Cover'); const colSize = modisCol.size().getInfo(); print(`MODIS Snow Images: ${colSize}`); // Check for empty collection if (colSize === 0) { print("No MODIS snow data found."); print("C1"); return; } // Create composite (max snow cover over the period) const composite = modisCol.max(); // Mask out non-snow values (101-255 are clouds/no data/water etc.) // Values 0-100 represent snow cover percentage const snowMasked = composite.updateMask(composite.lte(100)); // 3. Check valid pixels const pixelCount = snowMasked.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: deltaGeometry, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('NDSI_Snow_Cover').getInfo(); print(`Valid pixels after masking: ${pixelCount}`); if (pixelCount === 0 || pixelCount === null) { print("No valid snow pixels in region."); print("C2"); return; } // 4. Calculate mean snow cover const meanSnow = snowMasked.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: deltaGeometry, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('NDSI_Snow_Cover').getInfo(); print(`Mean snow cover (%): ${meanSnow}`); // 5. Validation & Final Answer if (meanSnow === null || meanSnow === undefined || meanSnow < 0 || meanSnow > 100) { print("Invalid snow cover value."); print("C3"); } else if (meanSnow > 0) { print("Snow detected in region."); print("A"); } else { print("No snow detected."); print("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
